steps.scene: You're behind a long lorry approaching a crossroads. It signals left — then swings out towards the right-hand side of the road.

options.text: Stay well back and give it room
Assume the signal is wrong and it's turning right
Move into the gap on its left as it slows

question.explanation: A long vehicle swings the opposite way first so its rear wheels clear the kerb. Any gap it opens will close as it turns.

steps.title: Why you sit back from a lorry
steps.body: The further back you are, the more of the road ahead you can see past it — and the more likely the driver is to see you in their mirrors.

question.prompt: Why keep well back while following a large vehicle?

options.text: Tucking in close gives you a better view past it
To get the best view of the road ahead
In case the vehicle stops and rolls backwards

question.explanation: Close behind a lorry you can see nothing but the lorry, and you sit in the driver's blind area.

steps.scene: You've left a good gap behind a lorry. A car pulls out of the queue beside you and drops straight into it.

options.text: Close up again so it can't happen twice
Flash your headlights at the car that cut in
Drop back further and rebuild the gap

question.explanation: The gap is your stopping room, not your property. Ease off and take it back calmly.

steps.scene: You're following a lorry on a soaking wet dual carriageway. Its spray is coating your windscreen and you can't read the road ahead.

options.text: Move closer, where there's less spray to deal with
Drop back until you can see properly again
Switch to full beam so you can see through it

question.explanation: Dropping back takes you out of the spray and buys stopping distance you badly need on a wet road.

steps.scene: A bus is stopped at a bus stop ahead of you, and people are getting off it onto the pavement.

question.prompt: What's the hazard as you pass?

options.text: Passengers will walk to a crossing before stepping out
Someone stepping into the road from behind the bus
The bus reversing back towards the stop

question.explanation: People cross straight from the front and back of a bus, hidden from you until the last moment.

steps.title: A bus signalling to pull out
steps.body: Give way to it when you safely can. Don't accelerate to get past, and don't flash it out — other road users read your lights too.

question.prompt: A bus at a stop signals to move away. What should you do?

options.text: Get past it before it starts to move
Let it pull away, if it's safe to do so
Signal left and wave the driver out

question.explanation: Letting a bus out costs you seconds. Squeezing past it puts you alongside as it moves off.

steps.wrongBelief: Sitting close behind a hesitant learner encourages them to get on with it.

question.prompt: The learner ahead of you stalls at a junction. What should you do?

options.text: Stay close behind and flash your headlights
Be patient — expect them to make mistakes
Steer around them and carry on

question.explanation: Pressure makes a nervous driver stall again. Hang back and give them the room to sort it out.

steps.repairNote: Learners react more slowly and make mistakes — that's the point of learning. Leave room and wait.
